_comment: Single source of truth for build-loop's two-axis model taxonomy. SEGMENT axis = work role / primary output; CAPABILITY-TIER axis = a 7-rung ladder. Read by scripts/model_taxonomy.py (the loader every other script imports). Anthropic/OpenAI ids are EXAMPLE SEEDS held as data, NOT hard-codes — classification appends new models to the runtime cache, never to this file. Provider names are illustrative. KISS/DRY: nothing here is duplicated in code.

fallback._comment: One-edge capability fallback walk on the GENERATIVE ladder T0..T5. T-S is specialist (off-ladder): it never participates in the capability fallback walk. The HARD FLOOR INVARIANT is enforced in code: a tier walks AT MOST one edge upward in capability, so T1/frontier never resolves below T2/thinking.

legacy_aliases._comment: The 4 legacy tier tokens map onto ladder rungs. Back-compat: config modelOverrides, plan tier: frontmatter, route_decision, and every existing test reference these tokens — normalize_tier folds them to the ladder so they keep resolving to the same models.

prompting_profiles._comment: Per-TIER prompting posture consulted automatically at dispatch: rides the resolve_agent_model.py envelope as `prompting_profile`. Keyed by capability rung (ADR-02, plan 2026-07-21-model-prompting-profile): a new model classified into a rung INHERITS its profile — freshness is structural, not calendar. `summary` is the INJECTION PAYLOAD -- actionable, self-contained, and safe to paste into a consumer project, so it carries no repo-internal jargon and never cross-references another rung. Epistemics live in `evidence_note` and `confidence`, never in `summary`. `confidence` is part of the data by design: `verified-source` = Anthropic Claude Code team claims, Willison transcript 2026-07-21; `repo-measured` = build-loop round-3 implementer-brief evidence; `weak` = the source EXPLICITLY declined to endorse the small-model half ('We haven't been able to eval it — we don't have any hard data'). Fields trace to named observed failures (neg-constraint gradient F2, invariant brief template F3, rationale-free directives F8); the transcript is explanation, not authority.

T0.summary: State the goal, the context, and the falsifier. Omit worked examples. Give every constraint its rationale. Trust the model with the edge cases.
T0.evidence_note: Source-verified against the Anthropic Claude Code team's 2026-07-21 published guidance. T0 shares T1's posture; no T0-specific evidence exists.

T1.summary: State the goal, the context, and the falsifier. Omit worked examples. Give every constraint its rationale. Trust the model with the edge cases.
T1.evidence_note: Source-verified against the Anthropic Claude Code team's 2026-07-21 published guidance.

T2.summary: Lead with context rather than directives. Include at most one compact example, and only when the contract is novel. Delegate the edge cases, but name the falsifiers you already know.
T2.evidence_note: Source-verified against the Anthropic Claude Code team's 2026-07-21 published guidance.

T3.summary: Write the full brief: worked contract examples, explicit caps with the arithmetic shown, and known edge cases enumerated (including schema-field warnings).
T3.evidence_note: examples and edge_case_handling are repo-measured at this rung; the remaining fields are inferred. This rigor is load-bearing here -- do not strip it.

T4.summary: Write the full explicit brief: worked examples and direct instructions.
T4.evidence_note: WEAKLY EVIDENCED PLACEHOLDER. This encodes what build-loop already does at this rung rather than a posture chosen on evidence; it exists so every ladder rung resolves. The source declined to endorse detailed-prompting-for-small-models without eval data. Revisit at the eval trigger.

T5.summary: Write the full explicit brief: worked examples and direct instructions. Use this rung for bounded mechanical tasks only.
T5.evidence_note: WEAKLY EVIDENCED PLACEHOLDER, same basis as T4.

preferred._comment: Ordered preferred-model list per (segment, tier). Order = capability rank, honoring Accuracy>Speed>Cost. The resolver picks the highest-ranked AVAILABLE + host-reachable id; ties / equal-or-unranked broken by release recency (newer wins). Users reorder via .build-loop/config.json. ALL 7 segments carry at least one cell so the data shape is uniform; dormant cells are data only — no resolver walks them yet.

models._comment: Seed registry: model id -> {provider, label, segment, tier, tags[], released (ISO date, for the recency tiebreak), status, aliases[]}. status: default (the segment/tier's host fallback) | verified (cross-vendor, advisory) | local | specialist. Runtime classification writes to .build-loop/model-tier-cache.json, NOT this file.

opus.label: Claude Opus 5
opus.spec_source: platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/models/whats-new-opus-5 + /pricing (verified 2026-07-25); dispatch token confirmed by activation probe 2026-07-28 (model: opus -> claude-opus-5[1m])
opus._tier_note: Promoted T2->T1 on 2026-07-28. Evidence: observations/2026-07-28-audit-bakeoff-fable-vs-opus5-vs-sonnet5.json — strict superset of the sitting T1 occupant (fable) in 3/3 adversarial-audit rounds, including reversing a defect fable had explicitly cleared. Scope limit: the evidence is verification-shaped (n=3, one repo, one task family, effort unpinned, not single-blind). It does NOT cover plan/spec authoring — see frontier_gate.py, which routes high-coupling planning back to fable until a spec-authoring bakeoff exists.

glm-5.2.label: GLM-5.2
glm-5.2.evidence: Terminal-Bench 2.1: 81.0 vendor-self-reported (z.ai) vs 67.8-78 independent — up to a 13pt spread on the benchmark most predictive of agentic terminal work. Context window disputed: z.ai says 1M, Together says 256K. 744-753B MoE, ~750GB FP8; server-only, no local option.

grok-4.6.label: Grok 4.6
grok-4.6.evidence: Terminal-Bench 2.1: 88.4 independent, BUT Terminal-Bench v3.0: 26%, ~8.6pt behind GPT-5.6 Sol. Same model, incomparable benchmark versions — reading 88.4 as frontier-agentic reads the wrong version. Real argument is efficiency: ~53 turns / 0.5B input tokens where Opus 5 took ~103 turns / 2.0B. That is a coordination argument, not a gating-verdict one.

gemini-3.7-flash.label: Gemini 3.7 Flash
gemini-3.7-flash.evidence: Terminal-Bench 2.1: 85.8 (DeepMind, corroborated by an independent leaderboard at the same value). Best price-per-agentic-point in this set at $0.75/$3.75. NOTE: intro pricing doubles to $1.50/$7.50 on 2027-01-01.

gemini-3.1-pro.label: Gemini 3.1 Pro
gemini-3.1-pro.evidence: SWE-bench Verified 80.6 only — a static patch benchmark, weak evidence for multi-turn agentic work. 2.7x the input price of 3.7 Flash for weaker agentic evidence.

deepseek-v4-pro.label: DeepSeek V4-Pro
deepseek-v4-pro.evidence: SWE-bench Verified 80.6 next to Terminal-Bench 2.1 50.19 — strong at patch generation, materially weaker at running an agent loop. Same trap as GLM. 1.6T MoE / 49B active; server-only.

qwen3.6-27b.label: Qwen3.6-27B
qwen3.6-27b.evidence: SWE-bench Verified 77.2, Terminal-Bench 2.0 59.3, LiveCodeBench v6 83.9 (all self-reported on the model card). Does NOT fit 16GB: ~16.8GB at Q4_K_M for weights alone before any KV cache.

kimi-k2.7-code.label: Kimi K2.7 Code
kimi-k2.7-code.evidence: Best open-weight tool-calling candidate here IF the vendor number replicates: MCPMark Verified 81.1 (vendor, ahead of Opus 4.8's 76.4), hallucination rate 65%->39%. Independent Terminal-Bench 2.1 is 67.04. 1T MoE / 32B active; server-only.

legacy_registry._comment: Back-compat VIEW for model_overrides.MODEL_REGISTRY. The legacy 4-token tier surface advertised a curated selectable-model list per tier (broader than a single capability rung — e.g. frontier accepted cross-vendor frontier-equivalents). These ordered id lists preserve that exact contract (--list-models, is_registered) while keeping ALL model ids in this one file. The precise per-(segment,tier) capability assignment lives in `models` + `preferred`; this is only the legacy advisory registry. First id per tier is the default.

classification_rubric._comment: Segment-appropriate benchmark hints the host LLM uses when classifying an unseen model into BOTH segment and tier. Generative segments grade on reasoning/coding benchmarks; specialist segments grade on their own metrics (recall/NDCG/WER/latency), NOT SWE-bench.
classification_rubric.generative_reasoning: SWE-bench Verified / ARC-AGI / GPQA Diamond — tier by where it lands vs the prior-gen frontier ceiling
classification_rubric.agentic_execution: SWE-bench Verified + tool-use accuracy + tau-bench / agentic-harness scores
classification_rubric.governance_evaluation: judge-agreement rate / classification F1 / moderation precision-recall
classification_rubric.realtime_interaction: WER (word error rate) / end-to-end latency ms / streaming stability
classification_rubric.perception_input: document-VQA / vision / audio / video understanding benchmarks
classification_rubric.primary_role_rule: A model with image/audio INPUT but whose PRIMARY job is reasoning is generative_reasoning with a multimodal-input TAG. Classify into perception_input / realtime_interaction / generative_media ONLY when that IS the primary product role.
classification_rubric.tag_axis: Tags are a third axis (orthogonal to segment+tier): long-context, agentic, multimodal-input, cost-sensitive, restricted, local, coding, fast, nano, edge.
